canonical_policy.name: Default persistence stack
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Default persistence is EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server/SqlServer provider; provider-specific concerns stay out of Application and Domain.

reviews.boundary_analysis: EF SQL Server selection, explicit replacement mechanism preservation and named scaffold placement already registered; do not silently infer all persistence behavior from ORM choice.

canonical_policy.name: Default validation/logging
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library; application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog as provider.

reviews.boundary_analysis: FluentValidation/ILogger Serilog baseline plus registration package and sinks-only-needed rule explicit; Console enough local does not force extra sinks.

- Decided: .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Controllers. Moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.

- Decided: Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the interactive API documentation and manual-testing surface for Development (`/swagger`); expose it outside Development only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.

- With `[ApiController]`, model-binding failures produce validation problem responses automatically.
- FluentValidation fits required application input, string/collection constraints, ranges, cross-property and conditional rules. Register validators with `FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions`; follow the project's established invocation pattern instead of adding a competing mechanism, and do not add deprecated automatic-validation integration packages.
- A syntactically valid request can still violate a use-case or domain rule; ordinary CRUD and workflow rules stay in the use-case layer unless an approved design chose a richer domain model.

Rules: outbound-dependency rules (`.claude/rules/0-core/backend-code.md`). Package choice (Microsoft resilience packages by default; direct Polly only as a documented exception; deprecated Polly integrations never): `add-dependency`. The Microsoft packages are built on Polly v8, but application code normally configures them through the `Microsoft.Extensions` resilience APIs.

Configure only the sinks and enrichers the project needs; a Console sink is enough for a simple local Development baseline. File, Seq, OpenTelemetry, or Elasticsearch sinks are options, not baseline dependencies, and numeric limits below are illustrative.

The `Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch` package is deprecated; use `Elastic.Serilog.Sinks` when Elasticsearch is the chosen log store. OTLP export is available through `Serilog.Sinks.OpenTelemetry` without the OpenTelemetry SDK.

canonical_policy.name: Backend testing stack/layout
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use NUnit; backend test projects live under backend alongside production projects; WebApplicationFactory is the baseline for ASP.NET Core integration tests; Testcontainers is conditional.

reviews.boundary_analysis: NUnit adapter/analyzer, FakeTimeProvider when useful, host test baseline and optional test containers already registered separately; no always-container implication.

A simple Domain of entities and enums needs no dedicated test project. Integration tests may exercise Application, Infrastructure, persistence, routing, DI, and serialization transitively through the host. Frontend tests stay inside the frontend workspace.

Workspace: `frontend/<Name>.Web/`. Run commands from the workspace directory. Install packages only through `add-dependency`.

| `dotnet-ef` (local or global .NET tool) | repository tool manifest | migration commands |

- Default: use in-process host integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication, DI, repositories, the ORM, or database persistence is what the test must prove.
- Default: use the actual database provider when relational or provider behavior matters (an isolated real-provider container is optional, not required); never claim provider fidelity from a test that runs on a different provider.
- Tests start from a known state and own their setup; they never depend on development seed data or on the order of other tests.

- Commit boundary: the commit-boundary implementation delegates to `AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync`; staged changes are the tracked changes of the shared context.
- Relational fidelity: the actual provider is SQL Server. EF Core InMemory, SQLite, or another provider does not establish SQL Server behavior.

- Default: keep backend production and test projects (`backend/<Name>.<Layer>/`), the frontend workspace (`frontend/<Name>.Web/`), and documentation (`docs/`) clearly separated as approved; never create a separate top-level tests directory.

canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use current stable Angular with compatible TypeScript/RxJS, standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless mode when supported, SCSS, Angular Material/CDK and Vitest.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Installed CLI help verification, selected-Node-compatible current release qualifier and Material-use preference already explicit/challenged. No web updating frozen version claims.

- **Delegated** — local, reversible, and does not materially change a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract, or observable behavior: decide and proceed.
- **Reserved** — requires approval: changing an accepted project/architecture decision; adopting a new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS, mediator-based organization, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, a project-wide Result model, microservices); adding a production project/layer or changing the project reference graph; changing persistence boundaries (for example several persistence contexts) or persistence technology; adding an infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed cache, search, external storage, external identity); adding a major library/framework or replacing approved baseline technology; introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction; changing authentication/authorization architecture; a breaking public API change or adopting API versioning; defining product behavior or tunable values not defined by product sources; changing a capability selection (also requires an ADR).
- Unclear case: any "yes" makes it Reserved — does it add, remove, or replace a dependency, framework, or infrastructure capability? change a project/layer/reference boundary? establish a convention other code must follow? change observable behavior or a public contract? become expensive to reverse once other code depends on it?
